firstWallets.glossary.def1: The secret that lets you sign transactions and move assets.
firstWallets.glossary.def10: A signature that lets a contract spend a token from your wallet.
firstWallets.glossary.def11: A scam that plants look-alike addresses in your history.
firstWallets.glossary.def2: A list of 12 or 24 words that can recreate the keys of a wallet. Also called seed phrase.
firstWallets.glossary.def3: A service where a company holds the keys for you.
firstWallets.glossary.def4: Holding your own keys, with no company in between.
firstWallets.glossary.def5: A wallet whose keys live on a device connected to the internet.
firstWallets.glossary.def6: A dedicated device that keeps keys offline and signs on the device.
firstWallets.glossary.def7: The public identifier where an asset can be received on a network.
firstWallets.glossary.def8: The blockchain on which a transfer happens. It must match between sender and receiver.
firstWallets.glossary.def9: Ethereum Virtual Machine: the technology shared by Ethereum and compatible networks.

firstWallets.shot.backup.cap: Figure 2. Seed phrase backup (photo of a test wallet). Never photograph or share this screen on your real wallet.
firstWallets.shot.backup.l1: Make sure nobody and no camera can see the screen.
firstWallets.shot.backup.l2: Write the words on paper in the numbered order shown (01 to 12).
firstWallets.shot.backup.l3: Tap Done only after copying all 12 words. The app may ask you to confirm them next.
firstWallets.shot.create.cap: Figure 1. Creating a new wallet. Names and menus change over time.
firstWallets.shot.create.l1: Download only from the official store page or site.
firstWallets.shot.create.l2: Choose how to create it: with Google, e-mail or Apple (access goes through your account) or with a seed phrase (you keep the words). This guide follows the seed phrase path.
firstWallets.shot.create.l3: Set the local password or PIN for this device.
firstWallets.shot.qrpay.cap: Figure 4. The wallet's Pay area, with QR code scanning and other services.
firstWallets.shot.qrpay.l2: See what is available: scan a QR code, online purchases, eSIMs, hotels in many countries and other services. Options change over time and with your country.
firstWallets.shot.qrpay.l3: To pay a Pix, choose scan QR code, scan the merchant's code and check the amount in reais and in stablecoin before confirming.
firstWallets.shot.receive.cap: Figure 3. Receive screen, with the address of each network.
firstWallets.shot.receive.l1: Tap Receive and choose to browse by Token (the asset) or by Network.
firstWallets.shot.receive.l2: Find the network the sender will use, such as Ethereum, Solana or BNB Chain. It must be the same one.
firstWallets.shot.receive.l3: Tap the copy icon to copy the address for that network.
firstWallets.shot.withdraw.cap: Figure 5. Withdrawal form on an exchange. Options and names differ between platforms.
firstWallets.shot.withdraw.l1: Choose the asset you want to withdraw.
firstWallets.shot.withdraw.l2: Choose the network. It must be one that your wallet supports for that asset.
firstWallets.shot.withdraw.l3: Paste the address copied from your own wallet and compare the first and last characters.
firstWallets.shot.withdraw.l4: Enter the amount and check the network fee shown.
firstWallets.shot.withdraw.l5: Confirm with your security codes. Blockchain transfers cannot be undone.

fw.bitget.h1: Step 1. Install and create the wallet
fw.bitget.h2: Step 2. Back up the recovery phrase
fw.bitget.h4: Everyday use: QR payments and card
fw.bitget.note: Do not confuse it with the Bitget exchange. The exchange is a custodial company, while the wallet is the self-custody app, even though they share a brand.
fw.bitget.p1: Bitget Wallet is a multi-network self-custody wallet. Its main appeal for Brazilian users is that, besides storing and swapping assets, it connects the stablecoin balance to everyday payments. According to the company's announcements, this includes paying by QR code through Pix, a card that spends USDC and USDT, and buying stablecoins by bank transfer through a partner. Availability, eligibility and fees depend on your account and country and can change, so check the app before counting on any feature.
fw.bitget.records: Spending crypto also creates history: each payment uses an asset that has a date, an amount and a value in reais. Keep those records, as in the first lesson.
fw.bitget.s1: Install the app only from the official store page or the official site, then choose to create a new wallet. Set a local password or PIN. The app offers creating with Google, e-mail or Apple, or with a seed phrase. Here we follow the seed phrase, the path where you keep the recovery yourself.
fw.bitget.s3: To receive an asset, pick the asset and the network, then copy the address or show the QR code. The address is public and safe to share; the recovery phrase never is.
fw.bitget.use.card.text: A card that spends USDC and USDT wherever major card networks are accepted. Check the fees, limits and verification requirements shown in the app, since the announcements do not detail them.
fw.bitget.use.card.title: Card
fw.bitget.use.onramp.text: A bank transfer on-ramp operated by a partner. As seen in the previous lesson, the payment goes to a third party, so compare the total cost and keep the receipts.
fw.bitget.use.onramp.title: Buying stablecoins by Pix
fw.bitget.use.qr.text: You scan a merchant's Pix QR code, the app uses your stablecoin balance, and the merchant receives through the rail it already uses. The company says eligible users can verify to unlock it, so expect a verification step. The Pay area also groups other services, such as online purchases, eSIMs and hotels in many countries, depending on availability.
fw.bitget.use.qr.title: QR payment
fw.custody.custodial.text: Convenient and recoverable through support, but it depends on the company: its rules, its availability and its security.
fw.custody.custodial.title: Custodial
fw.custody.p1: A wallet does not store coins. Assets live on the blockchain, and the wallet stores the private keys that allow you to move them. Whoever has the keys controls the assets. In a custodial account, such as an exchange, the company holds the keys and you hold a claim. In a self-custody wallet, you hold the keys and nobody can freeze, block or approve your transfers.
fw.custody.p2: Neither one is "the right one" for everything. A common approach is to keep on an exchange only what you are about to trade, and the rest in a wallet you control.
fw.custody.self.text: Full control and no permission needed, but the responsibility is yours: lose the recovery phrase and nobody can restore access.
fw.custody.self.title: Self-custody
fw.intro.p1: In the previous lesson, your crypto stayed on an exchange, which means it stayed on a company's books. This lesson is about the other side: a wallet that only you control. You will see what a wallet really is, how to choose one, how to protect the recovery phrase, how to bring assets from an exchange to it, and how to start using it day to day.
fw.intro.p2: The main example is Bitget Wallet, a self-custody wallet that also offers payments by QR code and its own card. It is an example, not a rule: the right wallet depends on the networks you use, and the later sections cover options for Solana and for EVM networks. The screens are placeholders for real screenshots, and every platform changes its menus over time.
fw.intro.p3: By the end you will be able to explain what self-custody means, protect a recovery phrase correctly, withdraw from an exchange to your wallet without losing funds, and recognize the most common wallet scams.
fw.others.evm.text: Wallets for Ethereum and compatible networks (such as Base, Arbitrum and Polygon). Rabby is known for showing a preview of what a transaction will do before you sign.
fw.others.evm.title: EVM networks: MetaMask and Rabby
fw.others.hw.text: Devices such as Ledger, Trezor and Tangem can be used together with many software wallets, keeping the keys offline. Buy only from the official maker.
fw.others.hw.title: Hardware wallets
fw.others.p1: Wallets are not interchangeable across ecosystems. A Solana address and an EVM address have different formats, and the same recovery phrase can create accounts on different networks. The best wallet for you depends on where you will use your assets.
fw.others.p2: These are examples and not recommendations. Features and security of each wallet change, and the same rules apply to all of them: official download, protected phrase, and a test transfer before the real one.
fw.others.sol.text: Wallets built around Solana, available as extension and mobile app, with support for Solana tokens and apps.
fw.others.sol.title: Solana: Phantom and Solflare
fw.safety.fake.text: Copies of popular wallets appear in stores and in ads. Install only from the maker's official links, and check the publisher.
fw.safety.fake.title: Fake apps and extensions
fw.safety.intro: Most wallet losses come from the user signing or revealing something, not from a break in the blockchain. These are the patterns that repeat.
fw.safety.phrase.text: No support, no airdrop and no "wallet validation" site ever needs your recovery phrase. Anyone asking for it is a scammer.
fw.safety.phrase.title: Anyone asking for the phrase
fw.safety.poison.text: Scammers send tiny transfers from addresses that look like ones you used, hoping you copy them from the history. Always copy the address from the original source.
fw.safety.poison.title: Address poisoning
fw.safety.sign.text: Connecting to a site is harmless, but signing can give a contract permission to spend your tokens. Read what you are approving, and revoke old approvals you no longer use.
fw.safety.sign.title: Signing without reading
fw.seed.do.text: Write it on paper (or metal) as soon as it is shown, check each word, keep it in a safe place, and consider more than one copy in separate places.
fw.seed.do.title: Do
fw.seed.dont.text: Do not take a screenshot, save it in notes, e-mail it, upload it to a cloud or type it into any website. Do not share it with anyone, including "support".
fw.seed.dont.title: Do not
fw.seed.p1: When you create a self-custody wallet, it shows a recovery phrase (also called seed phrase), usually 12 or 24 words. That phrase is the wallet: anyone who has it can recreate your keys on another device and move everything.
fw.seed.p2: A password or a PIN protects the app on one device. The recovery phrase protects the funds everywhere. After creating the wallet, send a small amount to it and practice restoring the wallet from the phrase on a clean install, so you know the backup works before it matters.
fw.summary.i1: A wallet stores private keys, not coins. Whoever holds the keys controls the assets.
fw.summary.i2: Custodial accounts depend on a company. Self-custody gives full control and full responsibility.
fw.summary.i3: Software wallets are practical and more exposed. Hardware wallets keep keys offline and suit larger amounts.
fw.summary.i4: The recovery phrase is the wallet. Write it on paper, never digitize it, never share it, and test the restore.
fw.summary.i5: Bitget Wallet is an example of a wallet that connects the stablecoin balance to QR payments and a card, subject to availability and verification.
fw.summary.i6: Different ecosystems use different wallets: for example Phantom and Solflare for Solana, MetaMask and Rabby for EVM networks.
fw.summary.i7: When withdrawing from an exchange, match the network, compare the address, and test with a small amount first.
fw.summary.i8: Be careful with anyone asking for the phrase, with fake apps, with blind signatures and with look-alike addresses.
fw.types.checks.i1: Who makes it, for how long, and whether the code is open or audited.
fw.types.checks.i2: Whether it supports the network and the tokens you want to use.
fw.types.checks.i3: Whether it is self-custody: you must receive a recovery phrase that only you hold.
fw.types.checks.i4: That the download comes from the official site or the official store page of the maker.
fw.types.cold.text: A dedicated device that keeps keys offline and signs transactions on the device itself. Better for larger amounts, but it costs money and must be bought from the official maker.
fw.types.cold.title: Hardware wallets (cold)
fw.types.hot.text: Mobile apps, desktop apps and browser extensions. Keys live on a device that is online, which is practical for daily use and exposed to malware and phishing.
fw.types.hot.title: Software wallets (hot)
fw.types.multi.text: One app that supports many blockchains. Convenient, but each network has its own address format and its own risks.
fw.types.multi.title: Multi-network wallets
fw.types.native.text: Wallets built around one ecosystem, such as Solana or EVM networks, usually with deeper support for its apps and tokens.
fw.types.native.title: Network-specific wallets
fw.types.p1: Wallets are usually grouped by how they connect to the internet and by who makes them.
fw.withdraw.p1: Now you can bring assets from an exchange to your wallet. The order matters: start with the wallet, copy the address for the right network, and only then go to the exchange.
fw.withdraw.rules.i1: The network on the exchange and the network of the address must be the same. The same asset can exist on several networks, and sending on the wrong one can mean losing the funds.
fw.withdraw.rules.i2: Compare the first and last characters of the address after pasting it. Some malware replaces copied addresses without you noticing.
fw.withdraw.rules.i3: For the first withdrawal, send a small amount and confirm that it arrived. Then send the rest.
fw.withdraw.rules.i4: Some exchanges let you save a list of allowed addresses. Turn it on after adding your own wallet.
